findings.note: The agent who should do the noting is absent; the construction hides behind an impersonal 'it'. The surrounding sentences do not name who is obliged to note this.
The clause does not name who clears the bus routes. The surrounding sentences name the contracts, not the party that performs the clearing.

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: The passive hides who made the decision to sell. Surrounding sentences name the author sitting at the table, but this clause never states the actor.
The noun "realization" carries the action, while the verb is the empty phrase "had come to". The verb buried in the noun is "realize".

findings.quote: The decision to sell was made
findings.note: "decision" is an action noun carried by "was made"; the verb "decide" is buried in the noun.
"evaluation" is an action noun carried by "carried out"; the verb "evaluate" is buried in the noun.

findings.quote: After eleven years of sitting in morning traffic behind a school bus,
findings.note: The introductory phrase before the subject runs fourteen words, placing the main subject 'I' late in the sentence.

findings.quote: By the time I reached the top of the hill that February,
findings.note: The introductory clause before the subject "I" runs thirteen words. The subject is "I".

findings.quote: It should be noted that I am not trying to tell anyone else how to live.
findings.note: The main subject "I" appears after thirteen words, counting the introductory clause "It should be noted that" before it.
"picturesque" appears twice within two sentences; the first occurrence is in the preceding sentence at "a picturesque row of Victorian houses".

findings.quote: I reached the bottom of the hill by seven.
findings.note: Three consecutive sentences are built on the same time-stamp template, opened by "I left the house at six-forty." and continued by this sentence.

findings.quote: a new bike and a new lock
findings.note: "bike" appears in the first sentence and again twice here, with a short intervening sentence.

findings.quote: which may or may not resemble yours
findings.note: The doubled pair "may or may not" states one hedge twice.
Doubled pair: "plain" and "simple" say the same thing. The pairing is the second item in a sentence that already contrasts walk and car.

findings.quote: A monthly bus pass costs sixty.
findings.note: The opening jumps to a new element, a bus pass, which the previous sentence about yearly car costs did not prepare. The link is only inferable from the contrast in price at the end of that sentence.

"The walk" opens on an element that the previous sentence did not name; that sentence was about having forgotten the distance could be covered another way. The reader can place the walk from the wider draft, but the link to the preceding sentence is only implicit.
The preceding sentences are about the narrator's morning walk and arrival; this sentence opens on an unrelated institutional subject, city snow contracts, with no transition.

findings.quote: My bike was stolen in June.
findings.note: The sentence opens on "My bike", a new element; the previous sentence was about the Fenwick Road bridge and crossing it on foot.

findings.quote: The combination was forgotten twice in the first week.
findings.note: "The combination" is a new element at the opening; the previous sentence was about buying a bike and a lock.

findings.quote: The car had been a warm cocoon
findings.note: The sentence opens on "The car", an element not mentioned in the previous sentence about walking and seeing the neighbourhood. The prior sentence was about the change wrought by walking.

findings.quote: an anchor that kept me moored to my own small concerns
findings.note: Mixed figure: the car is first a cocoon and then an anchor, and the two images cannot both hold. Nothing in the draft supplies the mechanism by which either one confines the narrator.

findings.quote: It should be noted that I am not trying to tell anyone else how to live. Everyone's situation is different, and what works for one person will not necessarily work for another. Many people live too far from work, or have children to drop off, or have jobs that require a car, and I do not want to suggest that any of them are doing anything wrong.
findings.note: Restatement and stacked qualification: the hedge that the writer is not prescribing anything is stated three times over, and "Everyone's situation is different" and "what works for one person will not necessarily work for another" make the same limit twice.
The reader cannot yet place 'that February'; the only February the draft establishes is supplied three paragraphs later, in 'The first winter was very hard.'

findings.quote: The first winter was very hard.
findings.note: 'The first winter was very hard.' resumes the winter walking already described in 'By the time I reached the top of the hill that February', with 'The decision to sell was made in April' and 'It should be noted that I am not trying to tell anyone else how to live' standing between them.
The verb "makes" carries the action noun "determination"; the verb "determine" exists.
The noun "review" carries the action while "conduct" does the grammatical work.
The draft never says who raised the concerns. It matters because the sentence is offered as evidence of a standing problem.
The clause hides who made the decision to route all changes through the board. Neither this sentence nor the surrounding ones names that actor.

findings.quote: Given the results of the pilot and what both teams told us in the May retrospective,
findings.note: 17 words precede the main subject "I".
"The board" opens three consecutive sentences (sentences 2-4).
Stock image standing in for the argument about the cost of a fixed monthly review. The draft never states what the constraint actually costs a team.

findings.quote: a toll booth on the highway to production
findings.note: Stock image standing in for the argument: it asserts obstruction without saying what the toll is, who pays it, or why the comparison holds.
"cumbersome" appears twice, the second time in "is cumbersome too" two sentences after the first occurrence in "Its checklist is cumbersome".
Doubled pair: "full and complete" says the same thing twice.
Restatement. The preceding sentence already reports the pilot results: the drop in median wait and the absence of rollbacks.

findings.quote: Oversight would remain in place for the changes where it matters most, and that point should not be lost.
findings.note: Restatement of the same reassurance about retained board review already given in the preceding sentence.
"The results" is a new element; the previous sentence was about the teams' median wait and rollbacks. The link to the prior sentence is only inferable at that sentence's end.
The previous sentence is about a Friday change waiting six days; this opens on an unnamed decision in 2023 with no shared term or transition.
The opening introduces admission controllers and the cluster, neither mentioned earlier; the previous sentence was about recording approvals in the release ticket.

The opening introduces approvals as a new element, while the previous sentence concerned the shortness of the pilot period. The connection to the previous sentence is not made until the mention of the audit trail.
The pilot and both teams are not introduced until the paragraph beginning 'In March and April, the Payments'.

The term 'high-risk change' depends on the high-risk list introduced in the paragraph beginning 'In March and April, the Payments'; earlier text names billing, authentication or customer data instead.

findings.quote: In March and April, the Payments
findings.note: This returns to the pilot introduced in the paragraph beginning 'Under the pilot, both teams' after the current-process and oversight paragraphs.
"decision" is the action noun and "made" is the empty verb carrying it; the deciding is buried in the noun.
"Undertaking" is an action noun carried by the empty verb "given"; the same clause also buries the action in "assessment" behind "carry out", leaving no working verb.
"Assessment" names the action while "carry out" does the grammatical work.

findings.quote: Flood warnings for Quay Street were not issued
findings.note: The draft never says who failed to issue the warnings; that body is responsible for the timing failure the paragraph turns on.
The promiser is not named anywhere in the paragraph, and the broken promise is the cost at issue.
The sentence opens on gluten development, a new element; the previous sentence was about Tom driving for flour. Nothing earlier in the paragraph prepares it.
The sentence opens on the hall kitchen, a new element; the previous sentence was about selling forty loaves from a trestle table.

findings.quote: The flood wall was built in 1962
findings.note: The previous sentence is about the police closing the street; the flood wall is a new element, and the link appears only in the later clause of this sentence. The reader reaches the wall with nothing prepared for it.
The doubled pair "each and every" states the same idea twice.
"sodden" appears twice within two sentences, first in "the smell of sodden flour".
Three consecutive sentences open with the same subject-verb template, following the same pattern in the first sentence, which begins "She rang".
"whole" appears twice within two sentences; the first occurrence is in "the whole street".
"heart" is repeated within the same sentence, first in "the beating heart" and again in "when a heart stops".

findings.quote: many people on Quay Street in many different ways
findings.note: "many" appears twice in the same clause.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways. Some lost stock and some lost income, and some lost things that are harder to put a price on. It is difficult to overstate how much the flood affected the people of the street, and it would be impossible to describe every way in which their lives were changed by it.
findings.note: Restatement. The passage repeats the point already made in the same paragraph's opening sentences about people losing stock, income and other things.
Stock image. It stands in for whatever the street is said to have learned, which the draft never states.

findings.quote: The bakery is the beating heart of Quay Street
findings.note: Stock image standing in for the claim that the bakery matters to the street. The draft supplies no mechanism or comparison the reader needs beyond the cliché itself.

findings.quote: lit a fire under the council
findings.note: Stock image that stands in for the argument about what pressure was applied and what the council did in response. The draft never states it.

findings.quote: The insurance payment, when it came in August,
findings.note: The account of the flood morning that begins in 'At a quarter past four on the ninth of March' is left for this August insurance outcome and resumes at 'She rang her son Tom'.

findings.quote: The flood affected many people on Quay Street in many different ways.
findings.note: Repeats the general claim about the flood's effect on the street already made in 'It was obviously a shock to the whole street'.
The clause does not say who would make the decision, even though the surrounding sentences only name the committee as having decided to make one.
The draft never says who conducted the meeting, so the reader cannot tell who is responsible for its conduct.
The draft never says who would make the determination.

findings.quote: a resolution would be arrived at
findings.note: The clause hides who would arrive at the resolution. The draft never names the actor.
The clause hides who tabled the matter. The chair is only implied, not stated.
"resolution" appears twice within the same two consecutive sentences (in the expectation clause and again in "No resolution was arrived at").
"feeling" appears twice in two sentences, first in the opening sentence of this paragraph.
"expectation" is buried behind "There was"; the action is expecting.
"observation" is buried behind "made"; the action is observing.
"Determination" is an action noun carried by "made". The verb "determine" exists, so the action is buried in the noun.
"Decision" names the action buried in the empty verb "made"; the clause already carries "was decided", so the actor disappears behind two action nouns.

findings.quote: It was decided by the committee that a decision would be made
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph opening 'It was decided by the committee thxt x determination would be made regarding the proposal'; it adds nothing.

findings.quote: There was an expectation that a resolution would be arrived at.
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph opening 'There was an expectation that'; it adds nothing.

findings.quote: Some of us left the room with the feeling that nothing had been accomplished.
findings.note: Repeats the earlier paragraph opening 'Some of us left the room with the feeling'; it adds nothing.
